newsitem.title: CANADA: Ford to hold annual meeting in Windsor, Ontario.
newsitem.headline: Ford to hold annual meeting in Windsor, Ontario.

text.p: Ford Motor Co. announced Tuesday that it will hold its annual shareholder meeting in Windsor, Ont., the first time the automaker has held the meeting outside of the United States since becoming a publicly traded company in 1956.

Windsor is located across the Detroit River from Detroit, not far from Ford's headquarters in nearby Dearborn, Mich. It is near the site where Ford Motor Co. of Canada, Ltd., began production in 1904 of the Ford Model C.

Ford of Canada is oldest operating auto company in Canada, according to Ford. The unit has 14,000 employees, with 5,700 in the Windsor operations. Those include the Windsor Engine Plant, Windsor Casting Plant, Essex Engine Plant, Essex Aluminum Plant, Windsor Aluminum Plant and an adjacent cast aluminum research development facility.

Ford's site selection follows several milestones for the Canadian operations. In 1996, Ford captured truck sales leadership for the first time and completed its most extensive plant investment programmes in our 93-year history, officials said.

"The selection of a Canadian location has historical significance because it was in Canada that Ford Motor Company began its expansion outside of the U.S. to more than 200 countries presently," Mark W. Hutchins, Ford of Canada's president and chief executive officer, said in a statement.
The meeting will begin at 10 a.m. on May 8 in the Cleary International Centre, Riverside Drive. Last year, Ford held its annual meeting in Kansas City, Mo.
Chrysler Corp. will hold its meeting May 15 in Seattle, Wash. General Motors Corp. has not released its annual meeting date and location. A spokesman could not be reached.
